To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MHC class II complexes are transported from the TGN directly to MIICs, and that cathepsin and MHC class I complexes are transported to MIICs in a Man-6- P independent pathway.
MHC class II and cathepsin-D containing vesicles are formed in the TGN and that they do not contain the Man-6-P receptor.

MHC class II and lysosomal hydroleses are delivered to early MIICs by vesicles that lack clathrin, the Man-6-P receptor and the mannose receptor, and that this transport pathway is independent of the mannose 6 phosphate recognition signal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the intracellular transport and biogenesis of MHC Class II molecules.
the molecular mechanisms that control the intracellular transport of lysosomal enzymes and MHC class I and class II proteins.
the biogenesis of MIICs in normal and ICD B lymphocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MHC class I and II compartments are formed by a process that does not involve clathrin coated vesicles.
the MHC class I and II molecules are transported from the Golgi apparatus to the endocytic compartment via a non clathrin coated vesicle.
the ICD B lymphocytes are deficient in the ability to sort newly synthesized lysosomal hydroleses from newly synthesized MHC class II.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ICD B cells have a defect in their endosomal system that is manifested as a failure to transport newly synthesized catheptin D to the endosome and a failure to transport MHC class II complexes to late endosomes.
the Man-6-P receptor is required for the formation of the MIICs, and that the Man- 6-P receptor is not required for the transport of MHC class I molecules from the TGN.
the I-cell B lymphoblast cell line is deficient for the Man-6-P receptor, but not for the Man- 6-P receptor-independent pathway for the transport of lysosomal enzymes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MHC classII compartment is not only a site of MHC classII processing but also a site of lysosomal enzyme sorting.
the MHC classII compartment (MIIC) is not a late endosome but a specialized organelle that forms by a Man- 6-P-independent process in the TGN.
the MHC classII compartment (MIIC) is a unique organelle in the secretory and endocytic pathways that is not a part of the classical endocytic pathway.
